name: input-group
purpose: Composition container that joins an input primitive with any number of adjacent controls (buttons, selects, static addons) into a single visual field (an input group, as other UI kits call it). The root only orchestrates: it draws the outer border, the `focus-within` ring, and applies inline Tailwind child-selectors so the first child rounds only on the left, the last only on the right, and internal borders collapse between siblings. Everything else is a **child**: the middle input is a raw `<input>` in the root's `default` slot; sibling controls (`<Button>`, `<Select>`, `<Input>`, or an `<InputGroup.Addon>` for static text like `https://` / `.com` / `$`) are dropped in directly alongside it. This is a breaking change from v3: the `#left` and `#right` named slots are gone — their static-text role moves to `<InputGroup.Addon>`, and their interactive role is served by placing the real component (`Button`, `Select`) as a direct child. Consumers therefore never wrap `Button`/`Select` in an inner `<div>` — the root's child selectors do that job.
useWhen: A text input that needs static prefix or suffix content inside the same border (`https://`, `.com`, a currency symbol).
An input joined to a control: a search field with a trailing `button`, an amount with a leading currency `select`.
avoidWhen: A phone number with a dial code → use `phone-input`.
A single input with only a decorative icon → use `input` and its `iconLeft` / `iconRight` slots.
related: `field` — wrap the group in a `Field` for a label and description/error; `InputGroup.Input` takes the field's id, `aria-describedby` and state, and the root takes `invalid` / `disabled` / `required` from it.
`phone-input` — input group with a dial-code select and a per-country mask.
`input` — the single-field primitive with icon slots.
bestPractices: Put static text and icons in `InputGroup.Addon`; place real controls (`button`, `select`) as direct children with no wrapper `div`.
Set the same `size` on the group and on its child controls so heights line up.

`disabled` and `invalid` on the group reach every field control inside (`InputGroup.Input`, `Input`, `Select` and the other controls that read the Field context); a `Button` or `IconButton` in the group needs its own `disabled`. `required` only mirrors to `data-required` on the group; set it on the input or on the enclosing `Field`, whose label carries the Required marker. Inside a `Field`, the Field's state reaches the root and the controls the same way.

Use `InputGroup.Input` for the middle input: it is borderless, picks up the enclosing `Field`'s wiring, and spares the long raw-`<input>` class string. An `Input` placed in the group loses its own border and radius (the group reads its `data-slot="input"`), so the group's frame and its dividers stay the only lines: the group never doubles a line.
The root is `role="group"`; label the inner input itself, or give the group an `aria-label`.

props.name: size
props.doc: Size token; affects the root's height and inner addon padding. Heights: small=28px, medium=32px, large=40px. Matches the sibling input primitives (`Input`, `Select`) — set the same `size` on child controls to keep them visually aligned.

props.name: invalid
props.doc: Renders the error border and marks the field controls inside invalid (`aria-invalid` on the input, never on the `role="group"` root, where ARIA does not allow it).

props.name: required
props.doc: Mirrors to `data-required` on the group and draws no border of its own. `aria-required` is not allowed on `role="group"`, so the required state belongs on the input (`InputGroup.Input` reads it from the Field).

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Renders the disabled visual, sets `aria-disabled="true"` on the root and disables the field controls inside (`InputGroup.Input`, `Input`, `Select`, …) through the Field context. A `Button` or `IconButton` inside needs its own `disabled`.

slots.name: default
slots.notes: On the **root**: the full row of children in visual order — any mix of `<InputGroup.Addon>`, `<Button>`, `<Select>`, `<Input>`, raw `<input>`. Order in the template is the order rendered left-to-right. On **`<InputGroup.Addon>`**: the addon content — text (`https://`, `.com`, `$`), an Azion icon `<i>`, or any small inline node; kept short by convention (long content breaks the fixed row height).
